24.01.01.context: A React workspace needs an Android companion.
24.01.01.concept: Capacitor hosts web content in a native shell; React Native renders native components. Compare reuse, native UX and plugin dependencies.
24.01.01.exercise: Draw the two runtime paths and identify the bridge boundary for a camera request.
24.01.01.positive: A choice is justified by measured requirements.
24.01.01.negative: Treating the native bridge as an ordinary unrestricted browser API fails.
24.01.01.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.02.context: A Vite SPA must load inside a mobile shell.
24.01.02.concept: A mobile entrypoint bundles static assets; native webDir must match build output and remote API origins must be explicitly configured.
24.01.02.exercise: Build a disposable Vite app, inspect output, configure the native shell and test offline startup.
24.01.02.positive: The bundled UI opens without a development server.
24.01.02.negative: A production build depending on localhost or exposing secrets fails.
24.01.02.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.03.context: A webview asks for a camera capability.
24.01.03.concept: Native bridge calls extend privileges beyond browser JavaScript; constrain origin, commands and inputs.
24.01.03.exercise: Run bridgeAllowed with trusted and foreign origins; on a real device exercise a denied plugin capability.
24.01.03.positive: Only the expected origin and command pass the model.
24.01.03.negative: A remote or unrecognized command receives no privilege.
24.01.03.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.04.context: An Android app is backgrounded during an edit.
24.01.04.concept: Lifecycle transitions may interrupt asynchronous work; persist intent before relying on in-memory state.
24.01.04.exercise: In a disposable app edit a task, background and terminate it; relaunch and reconcile the queue.
24.01.04.positive: The persisted edit survives and resumes once.
24.01.04.negative: Lost or duplicate work after process death fails.
24.01.04.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.05.context: An iOS app needs to be installed on a test device.
24.01.05.concept: Signing ties an app identity to an authorized provisioning path; simulator success is not a signed-device result.
24.01.05.exercise: List bundle ID, entitlement and provisioning requirements; use a permitted development account for device testing.
24.01.05.positive: A signed development build is attributable to the correct identity.
24.01.05.negative: Sharing signing private keys or claiming simulator success proves device signing fails.
24.01.05.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.06.context: A mobile app requests access to photos and network.
24.01.06.concept: Permissions should be minimal, contextual, and degrade safely when denied.
24.01.06.exercise: Request one scoped permission in a disposable app and test denial, revocation and retry.
24.01.06.positive: Allowed operation succeeds and denial is recoverable.
24.01.06.negative: Unnecessary broad storage permission or crash on denial fails.
24.01.06.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.07.context: An application stores an authentication token.
24.01.07.concept: Keep sensitive credentials in platform-backed secure storage; protect refresh, logout and expiry behavior.
24.01.07.exercise: Use synthetic tokens in a device secure-storage plugin; test logout and reinstall behavior with documented platform limits.
24.01.07.positive: Token is inaccessible to unrelated app code and logout clears intended state.
24.01.07.negative: Plain-text localStorage or logs holding a refresh token fails.
24.01.07.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.01.08.context: A learner packages a first Android application.
24.01.08.concept: Native build requires a reproducible toolchain, app identity, permissions, and signed or debug artifact distinction.
24.01.08.exercise: Build a disposable Capacitor APK with the actual Android toolchain, inspect manifest and install on an authorized test device.
24.01.08.positive: APK launches, reports correct version and handles permission denial.
24.01.08.negative: A web build alone is not APK acceptance.
24.01.08.boundary: Native builds, WebView isolation and plugin permissions require a real device.

24.02.01.context: A field worker edits tasks without internet.
24.02.01.concept: Local SQLite schema needs stable IDs, version, deletion marker and pending operations; transactionally write changes and queue intent.
24.02.01.exercise: Create a disposable SQLite schema and insert a synthetic task and queue row in one transaction.
24.02.01.positive: Both local record and operation persist together.
24.02.01.negative: Partial write after simulated failure violates the invariant.
24.02.01.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.02.context: A reconnect replays an already accepted edit.
24.02.02.concept: Stable operation IDs bind immutable operation content to deduplication; retry the same operation, not a new ID.
24.02.02.exercise: Run applyOperation for an edit twice then reuse its ID with changed content.
24.02.02.negative: Same ID with changed content conflicts.
24.02.02.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.03.context: Two devices edit the same task version.
24.02.03.concept: Conflict policy must be explicit: reject stale version, merge defined fields, or reconcile with user input. Last-writer-wins can lose data.
24.02.03.exercise: Apply version 0 edit then another version 0 edit; specify UI reconciliation for rejection.
24.02.03.positive: The accepted version advances and conflict is surfaced.
24.02.03.negative: Silently overwriting the first edit fails.
24.02.03.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.04.context: A device downloads a partial change feed.
24.02.04.concept: Cursors must belong to a defined stable ordering and scope; checkpoint only after applying a complete page.
24.02.04.exercise: Design an ordered synthetic feed with page size two and a crash before cursor commit.
24.02.04.positive: Replay does not skip or duplicate applied changes.
24.02.04.negative: Advancing cursor before data persistence loses records.
24.02.04.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.05.context: A deleted task is present on an offline device.
24.02.05.concept: Tombstones preserve deletion history until replicas have safely passed the relevant watermark.
24.02.05.exercise: Run the tombstone test, then attempt a stale update from an earlier version.
24.02.05.positive: The stale update is refused and deletion remains.
24.02.05.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.06.context: A device cache contains confidential workspace data.
24.02.06.concept: Encrypt sensitive offline data where appropriate, scope it to the signed-in actor and define logout/remote-revocation limits.
24.02.06.exercise: Create synthetic per-account cache partitions; switch users and inspect old account access.
24.02.06.positive: New user cannot read the prior user's data.
24.02.06.negative: Shared cache or plaintext secrets fail review.
24.02.06.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.07.context: A connection repeatedly drops during synchronization.
24.02.07.concept: Bound retries, use backoff and stable IDs, and preserve acknowledgements across reconnects.
24.02.07.exercise: Simulate request timeout after server accepts an operation; replay same ID and reconcile acknowledgement.
24.02.07.negative: Creating a new ID on retry causes duplicate work.
24.02.07.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.02.08.context: A learner edits and deletes tasks on two disconnected clients.
24.02.08.concept: An offline sync lab needs durable local writes, conflict handling, tombstones and authenticated server reconciliation.
24.02.08.exercise: Rehearse edit, replay, delete and stale resurrection using the model; then implement same cases with SQLite and a disposable API.
24.02.08.positive: Model invariants hold; actual restart test is recorded separately.
24.02.08.negative: Lost queue data or stale resurrection blocks real acceptance.
24.02.08.boundary: In-memory sync model; actual SQLite persistence, durable queue, crash recovery and conflict reconciliation are not established.

24.03.01.context: A desktop UI needs to read one local file.
24.03.01.concept: Tauri separates webview UI from Rust/native commands; treat each invocation as a privileged API.
24.03.01.exercise: Map read-document command from UI to Rust validation and returned DTO.
24.03.01.positive: Only documented command and scoped data cross the boundary.
24.03.01.negative: Arbitrary shell or path access from webview fails.
24.03.01.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.02.context: A Rust command receives malformed JSON.
24.03.02.concept: Rust types and Result errors are useful but do not replace input and authorization checks.
24.03.02.exercise: Implement a small typed command in a disposable Tauri app; send valid and invalid payloads.
24.03.02.positive: Valid payload returns a typed response; invalid input has a safe error.
24.03.02.negative: Panic, secret leakage or unchecked path fails.
24.03.02.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.03.context: A preview window tries to call a main-window command.
24.03.03.concept: Capabilities should scope window identities, plugins and commands to minimum privileges.
24.03.03.exercise: Use desktopAllowed for main/read then preview/read; inspect real capability configuration separately.
24.03.03.negative: Giving all windows the same unrestricted access fails.
24.03.03.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.04.context: A desktop app imports a user-selected document.
24.03.04.concept: Prefer a native file picker and bounded paths; validate type, size and symlinks at native boundary.
24.03.04.exercise: Select a synthetic file and try an out-of-scope path in an isolated app.
24.03.04.negative: Path traversal or arbitrary file overwrite fails.
24.03.04.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.05.context: An update downloads a replacement executable.
24.03.05.concept: Update trust requires signed artifacts and verified metadata; TLS alone does not establish artifact authenticity.
24.03.05.exercise: Design test signing keys and rehearse valid versus tampered update on disposable platform build.
24.03.05.positive: Tampered artifact is refused before install.
24.03.05.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.06.context: A desktop workspace must survive restart.
24.03.06.concept: SQLite supports local transactions; schema migration and storage location must be explicit per user.
24.03.06.exercise: Create a temporary DB, write a task, restart and verify migration/reopen.
24.03.06.positive: Record survives restart and schema remains compatible.
24.03.06.negative: Writing into installer directory or losing data fails.
24.03.06.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.07.context: A Windows app needs an installer or portable build.
24.03.07.concept: Packaging depends on target architecture, webview/runtime prerequisites and signing; build on supported toolchains.
24.03.07.exercise: Produce a real development artifact and inspect version, target and dependency requirements.
24.03.07.positive: Artifact launches on a clean authorized test machine.
24.03.07.negative: Merely zipping source or inventing signing evidence fails.
24.03.07.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.03.08.context: A learner ships a small desktop task app.
24.03.08.concept: End-to-end desktop acceptance covers native permissions, local persistence, packaging and uninstall behavior.
24.03.08.exercise: Run desktopAllowed, then implement a scoped file read and SQLite task flow in a disposable Tauri project.
24.03.08.positive: Allowed task flow works and forbidden window invocation fails.
24.03.08.negative: Missing installer or native test remains not-run.
24.03.08.boundary: Synthetic command permission model; actual Rust commands, capability enforcement, installers and signatures require platform builds.

24.04.01.context: A phone user struggles to tap tightly spaced controls.
24.04.01.concept: Touch targets, safe areas, orientation and text scaling must be tested on representative devices.
24.04.01.exercise: Build a synthetic form and test portrait, landscape, enlarged text and keyboard overlap.
24.04.01.positive: Controls remain reachable and labels readable.
24.04.01.negative: Clipping, tiny targets or obscured submit fails.
24.04.01.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.02.context: A mobile app sends task reminders.
24.04.02.concept: Push tokens identify installations, not user authorization; consent, token refresh and notification privacy matter.
24.04.02.exercise: Design synthetic push registration and revocation; use a permitted test provider to send one notification.
24.04.02.positive: Intended authorized device receives a minimal message.
24.04.02.negative: Cross-user delivery or confidential lockscreen content fails.
24.04.02.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.03.context: A sync process expects background work to run forever.
24.04.03.concept: Mobile OS scheduling is constrained; persist work and tolerate delayed or killed execution.
24.04.03.exercise: Queue two edits, acknowledge one, terminate app and call resumeQueue on persisted IDs.
24.04.03.negative: Assuming a background timer guarantees completion fails.
24.04.03.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.04.context: A link opens an authenticated workspace screen.
24.04.04.concept: Deep links need verified scheme/domain, validated parameters and authorization after routing.
24.04.04.exercise: Test a known task link, unknown ID and foreign-tenant link in a disposable app.
24.04.04.negative: Link payload bypassing authentication or tenant checks fails.
24.04.04.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.05.context: A mobile app drains battery after idle.
24.04.05.concept: Measure wakeups, network activity, heap and binary size under controlled conditions rather than guessing.
24.04.05.exercise: Record baseline on a test device, disable redundant polling, compare battery/network/size measurements.
24.04.05.positive: Work decreases without missed required updates.
24.04.05.negative: One unrepresentative measurement or broken sync fails.
24.04.05.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.06.context: A screen-reader user navigates a mobile form.
24.04.06.concept: Accessible names, roles, focus, text scaling and gesture alternatives need real assistive technology review.
24.04.06.exercise: Test a synthetic form with TalkBack or VoiceOver plus large text and keyboard where applicable.
24.04.06.positive: All fields and errors are announced in logical order.
24.04.06.negative: Unlabeled icon, focus trap or truncated error fails.
24.04.06.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.07.context: A learner prepares a store submission.
24.04.07.concept: Store policies, signing and disclosures are platform-specific and change; verify actual current requirements at release.
24.04.07.exercise: Create a release checklist for package identity, permissions, privacy, screenshots, target platform and testing.
24.04.07.positive: Each item links to actual current platform evidence.
24.04.07.negative: A debug APK is not proof of store approval.
24.04.07.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

24.04.08.context: A task disappears after airplane mode and relaunch.
24.04.08.concept: Queue durability requires distinguishing sent, acknowledged and locally applied work.
24.04.08.exercise: Use resumeQueue to replay only unacknowledged IDs; reproduce network loss and restart in actual app.
24.04.08.positive: Pending operation is retained until confirmed.
24.04.08.negative: Dropping work merely because a send was attempted fails.
24.04.08.boundary: Synthetic queue acknowledgement model only; physical touch, OS background behavior, push delivery and store acceptance require device tests.

25.01.01.context: A transactional app runs expensive monthly reports.
25.01.01.concept: OLTP optimizes short operational transactions; OLAP scans and aggregates analytical data. Separate workloads when measurements justify it.
25.01.01.exercise: Compare point lookup with a synthetic event aggregation and outline an isolated reporting path.
25.01.01.positive: Operational queries stay bounded and analytics has defined freshness.
25.01.01.negative: Heavy reporting starving production writes fails.
25.01.01.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.02.context: A dashboard recomputes totals on every refresh.
25.01.02.concept: Aggregations summarize a defined grain; materialized views persist results with a refresh/freshness contract.
25.01.02.exercise: In disposable PostgreSQL aggregate event counts and refresh a materialized view after new events.
25.01.02.positive: Reported totals match the stated refresh point.
25.01.02.negative: Assuming materialized results are always current fails.
25.01.02.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.03.context: An analytics SDK retries a page-view event.
25.01.03.concept: Event IDs, version, timestamp and consent scope are part of the instrumentation contract.
25.01.03.exercise: Run aggregateEvents with duplicate view ID and distinct purchase ID; document schema and consent.
25.01.03.positive: Exact duplicate is counted once in the model.
25.01.03.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.04.context: A company integrates several source systems into reporting.
25.01.04.concept: Warehouse layers separate ingestion, cleaning and consumption; define grain, lineage and late arrivals.
25.01.04.exercise: Sketch raw, staging and curated tables for synthetic orders; define unique source IDs.
25.01.04.positive: One curated order has traceable source and timestamp.
25.01.04.negative: Joining different grains and double-counting revenue fails.
25.01.04.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.05.context: A large event table needs column-oriented queries.
25.01.05.concept: ClickHouse is designed for analytical workloads; table engine, sorting key and ingestion shape influence performance.
25.01.05.exercise: In an isolated ClickHouse instance create a synthetic event table and compare filtered aggregates under documented conditions.
25.01.05.positive: Aggregate results match the known dataset.
25.01.05.negative: A claimed performance gain without actual comparable run fails.
25.01.05.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.06.context: A reporting transformation changes a revenue definition.
25.01.06.concept: dbt models version SQL transformations with dependency graphs and data tests; separate business definitions from source cleanup.
25.01.06.exercise: Build a disposable dbt model with unique/not-null tests and a documented revenue definition.
25.01.06.positive: Compiled SQL and tests agree with expected fixtures.
25.01.06.negative: Changing definition silently or failing data tests blocks release.
25.01.06.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.07.context: A pipeline receives missing IDs and negative amounts.
25.01.07.concept: Data quality assertions enforce uniqueness, nullability, accepted ranges and relationship contracts.
25.01.07.exercise: Inject duplicate IDs, missing IDs and invalid amounts into synthetic staging; write explicit reject/quarantine rules.
25.01.07.positive: Valid rows pass; bad rows have traceable disposition.
25.01.07.negative: Silently dropping or accepting corrupt rows fails.
25.01.07.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.01.08.context: A learner creates an event dashboard.
25.01.08.concept: Metric grain, deduplication, freshness and privacy must be visible alongside charts.
25.01.08.exercise: Use aggregateEvents on fixed synthetic events; build real query/dashboard only in disposable DB and reconcile totals.
25.01.08.positive: Dashboard count matches known event population.
25.01.08.negative: Inflated duplicates or hidden freshness delay fails.
25.01.08.boundary: In-memory count/deduplication model; no warehouse, materialized-view freshness, ClickHouse or dbt runtime qualification.

25.02.01.context: A workspace adds a text assistant.
25.02.01.concept: Application primitives separate model calls, streaming, tools and structured outputs; validate outputs before acting.
25.02.01.exercise: Design a typed read-only answer flow with source IDs and explicit error handling; use mock model response.
25.02.01.positive: UI receives a bounded answer and citations.
25.02.01.negative: Unvalidated tool call or secret in prompt fails.
25.02.01.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.02.context: A solo developer has a limited inference budget.
25.02.02.concept: Model selection balances task accuracy, latency, context and cost; evaluate against a fixed corpus and caps.
25.02.02.exercise: Define 20 synthetic evaluation questions, compare candidate models only with approved test budget and record actual usage.
25.02.02.positive: Selected model meets evaluation threshold within budget.
25.02.02.negative: Choosing solely by brand or unbounded retries fails.
25.02.02.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.03.context: A retrieved document instructs the model to reveal another tenant's records.
25.02.03.concept: Retrieved text is untrusted data, not authority; enforce retrieval ACLs and tool authorization outside the model.
25.02.03.exercise: Insert synthetic malicious instructions in a document; reject foreign citations with citedAnswer and verify tool denial separately.
25.02.03.positive: Foreign data and unauthorized tool calls are denied.
25.02.03.negative: Prompt instructions overriding access policy fails.
25.02.03.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.04.context: An assistant searches semantic document vectors.
25.02.04.concept: Embeddings represent text numerically; model/version/dimension and tenant metadata belong to the index contract.
25.02.04.exercise: In disposable PostgreSQL with pgvector, store synthetic vectors and query with tenant filter; test wrong dimension.
25.02.04.negative: Cross-tenant retrieval or mismatched dimension fails.
25.02.04.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.05.context: A large handbook must be retrieved in useful sections.
25.02.05.concept: Chunking trades context coherence against search granularity; preserve source and offsets and measure retrieval recall.
25.02.05.exercise: Split synthetic handbook by headings, compare chunks for fixed questions and track source IDs.
25.02.05.positive: Relevant sections are retrieved with traceable source.
25.02.05.negative: Chunks without provenance or missing relevant section fails.
25.02.05.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.06.context: An AI answer appears fluent but is unsupported.
25.02.06.concept: Evaluation datasets contain expected facts, source relevance, refusal cases and adversarial inputs; avoid using only happy paths.
25.02.06.exercise: Create labeled synthetic questions including unknown and foreign-tenant cases; score retrieval and answer separately.
25.02.06.negative: A citation string alone cannot count as factual correctness.
25.02.06.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.07.concept: Fallback routing must retain safety policy, output schema, deadline and budget across providers.
25.02.07.exercise: Simulate timeout and one bounded fallback with mock models; verify citations and output schema.
25.02.07.positive: Fallback preserves policy and records actual usage.
25.02.07.negative: Retry loops, unsafe fallback or silent cost increase fails.
25.02.07.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.02.08.context: A learner builds a source-cited assistant.
25.02.08.concept: Retrieval must be authorized before generation; sources must actually support claims and unknown answers should abstain.
25.02.08.exercise: Run citedAnswer membership checks, then build disposable retrieval pipeline and manually compare answer claims with sources.
25.02.08.positive: Allowed citations exist and real grounding is reviewed separately.
25.02.08.boundary: Synthetic citation membership check; not evidence of factual grounding, model safety, embeddings or real provider behavior.

25.03.01.context: A search endpoint stores point locations.
25.03.01.concept: Geometry uses a coordinate reference system; geography models geodetic distances. Document SRID and longitude/latitude order.
25.03.01.exercise: Create disposable PostGIS points with SRID 4326; compare distance behavior for geometry/geography.
25.03.01.positive: Coordinates and units match documented query.
25.03.01.negative: Mixing degrees and meters without conversion fails.
25.03.01.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.02.context: A map query scans all locations.
25.03.02.concept: Spatial indexes accelerate supported spatial predicates; verify with EXPLAIN and realistic data distribution.
25.03.02.exercise: Create synthetic points and GiST index; compare query plan for bounded spatial predicate.
25.03.02.positive: Plan and results are captured on same data.
25.03.02.negative: Index existence alone is not performance proof.
25.03.02.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.03.context: A user searches within a radius.
25.03.03.concept: Bounding boxes approximate candidate regions; exact distance predicate determines radius membership.
25.03.03.exercise: Construct inside/outside/edge cases and compare ST_DWithin with a bounding-box filter.
25.03.03.positive: Inside points included, outside excluded using correct units.
25.03.03.negative: Treating box corners as exact circle matches fails.
25.03.03.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.04.context: A map client loads visible results.
25.03.04.concept: Client should query bounded viewport, cluster or paginate results, and preserve accessible non-map alternatives.
25.03.04.exercise: Use a synthetic point list and viewport filter in a local map client; test narrow screen and keyboard alternative.
25.03.04.positive: Visible bounded points and accessible list agree.
25.03.04.negative: Fetching all private coordinates or inaccessible map-only UI fails.
25.03.04.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.05.concept: Coordinates must be finite and within expected range; validate order, SRID and size server-side.
25.03.05.exercise: Run validPoint with valid, swapped invalid, NaN and out-of-range values.
25.03.05.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.06.context: An app evaluates entry into a geographic zone.
25.03.06.concept: Geofence semantics need boundary rules, accuracy uncertainty, coordinate system and authorization.
25.03.06.exercise: In disposable PostGIS define a synthetic polygon, test inside/outside/boundary and accuracy tolerance.
25.03.06.positive: Chosen boundary rule is explicit and repeatable.
25.03.06.negative: Treating uncertain position as exact or bypassing permission fails.
25.03.06.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.07.context: A map exposes exact home locations unnecessarily.
25.03.07.concept: Location data can be sensitive; minimize precision, retention and audience, and obtain appropriate consent.
25.03.07.exercise: Use synthetic coordinates; compare coarse display with restricted exact record and deny foreign tenant access.
25.03.07.positive: Public view contains only approved precision.
25.03.07.negative: Precise private location leaks or persistent tracking fails.
25.03.07.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.03.08.concept: A geospatial search combines validated points, scoped query, correct distance and bounded result count.
25.03.08.exercise: Run validPoint; build disposable PostGIS search with known distance fixtures and map/list UI.
25.03.08.positive: Returned authorized points meet radius and ordering contract.
25.03.08.negative: Foreign locations, invalid points or unbounded results fail.
25.03.08.boundary: Coordinate validation model only; real PostGIS geometry, index, map rendering and location privacy require separate acceptance.

25.04.01.context: A private video needs efficient object delivery.
25.04.01.concept: Object storage owns bytes; CDN caches representations under defined authorization and freshness policies.
25.04.01.exercise: Design private object and public thumbnail paths with scoped cache policy; test synthetic unauthorized access.
25.04.01.positive: Private object is denied without authorized capability.
25.04.01.negative: Shared cache exposing protected media fails.
25.04.01.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.02.context: A video player experiences changing bandwidth.
25.04.02.concept: Adaptive streaming selects renditions from a manifest based on measured bandwidth and buffer; packaging and codecs matter.
25.04.02.exercise: Generate synthetic local media renditions with an authorized sample; inspect manifest and test switching in a real player.
25.04.02.positive: Playback remains coherent when bandwidth changes.
25.04.02.negative: Invalid segments or unsupported codec fails.
25.04.02.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.03.context: An uploaded file triggers a thumbnail job.
25.04.03.concept: FFmpeg processing untrusted inputs needs isolation, resource limits, timeouts and safe argument passing.
25.04.03.exercise: Run mediaAllowed with exceeded pixel limit; then test a sandboxed worker on synthetic media.
25.04.03.positive: Oversized input rejected before work; valid sample produces bounded output.
25.04.03.negative: Arbitrary shell arguments or unbounded decoding fails.
25.04.03.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.04.context: Two browsers need a live voice connection.
25.04.04.concept: WebRTC media transport depends on signaling, ICE/STUN/TURN, permissions and network conditions; SFU is a separate component.
25.04.04.exercise: In isolated browser test two synthetic peers and authorized room tokens; exercise blocked permission and reconnect.
25.04.04.positive: Authorized peers connect and denied participant cannot join.
25.04.04.negative: Assuming direct connectivity always works or public room access fails.
25.04.04.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.05.context: A private media URL is forwarded to another user.
25.04.05.concept: Signed URLs are scoped bearer capabilities with short expiry; authorization must precede issuance and cache policy must respect it.
25.04.05.exercise: Design synthetic object ID, expiry and audience policy; test expired and wrong-object capability in a real local signer.
25.04.05.positive: Valid scoped capability retrieves intended object.
25.04.05.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.06.context: A media service receives abusive or unsafe uploads.
25.04.06.concept: Quarantine, review policy, rate limits, appeals and audit trails are distinct from automated classification.
25.04.06.exercise: Model synthetic moderation states pending, approved, blocked with explicit reviewer access and error handling.
25.04.06.positive: Only approved allowed media is published.
25.04.06.negative: Scanner failure treated as approval or unreviewed public upload fails.
25.04.06.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.07.context: A free-tier project must estimate video costs.
25.04.07.concept: Estimate storage bytes, transfer, transcoding and concurrent streaming; validate current provider pricing separately.
25.04.07.exercise: Use hypothetical media sizes and views, calculate scenario ranges and identify hard resource caps.
25.04.07.positive: Costs include transfer and processing assumptions.
25.04.07.negative: Ignoring egress or quoting assumed prices as current fails.
25.04.07.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.

25.04.08.context: A learner builds asynchronous thumbnail processing.
25.04.08.concept: Durable job IDs, quarantine, bounded decoding, idempotent output and retry limits protect the worker.
25.04.08.exercise: Run mediaAllowed; implement a local disposable worker using authorized sample file and record retry/duplicate behavior.
25.04.08.positive: One bounded thumbnail output per job; errors tracked.
25.04.08.negative: Oversized, timed-out or duplicate job cannot create uncontrolled work.
25.04.08.boundary: Synthetic resource-bound model; no actual FFmpeg sandbox, CDN, HLS, WebRTC or moderation service acceptance.
